Knowledge reigns, wisdom gained

Black raincoat, shadow laps the curb in drizzle

Quarter-store hustle, not much but sold soul
Old man on the stoop, recounts glory with glare
From jazz clubs lowlit to church steps in prayer
Alphabet wall tags, wordweights, philosophy in graff
Paperboys with tomorrow folded under one hand's grasp
Broadcast static—spirituals round corners bend
Tragedy’s currency: schoolyard, fake friends

Lingering incense, stained glass-bounced rays

Pulled between hustle and the echoes of books
Empires left dusty, leaders bought with looks
Fist closed on dollar, open palm for the youth
Truth’s rare commodity, pawned off on the stoop
Neighborhood justice—too few hands involved
Unwritten economics, problems never solved
Cops chalk the outline, blue tape unfurls
Still, lessons rise nightly from alleyworld
